name: PFC Jones
role: PFC; with Larry around the helicopters
summary: Larry names a Jones several times. His son reports that Larry believes the man working at the rotor head in VN-0012 is PFC Jones, and later Larry said of that photograph: "Jones is looking at a bullet hole in the rotor which causes vibration. the helicopter was vibrating really bad." In VN-0020 he names the man in the white T-shirt: "Right, white t-shirt is PFC Jones." Of Sarge the monkey: "The monkey may have belong to Jones, the helicopter pilot." And on 2026-09-05: "PFC Jones and I got shot down and had to go back to the base and land one time. That is what PFC Jones was looking at in the picture."
researchNotes: Whether the PFC and "the helicopter pilot" are one man loosely described or two Joneses is unresolved; an enlisted crew chief would fit the rotor-head work and climbing into the Huey, and crew chiefs flew. Jones is too common for a blind roster search without the unit or a first name. 2026-09-05 (giscus-vn-0071-c18307913): the shoot-down comment was posted on VN-0071, but "what PFC Jones was looking at in the picture" most likely means VN-0012, where on 2026-09-03 Larry said Jones is looking at a bullet hole in the rotor (giscus-vn-0012-c18259673); corrected 2026-09-14 after research/site-audit-2026-09-14.md, which found the record had tied the event to VN-0071. A shoot-down that ended in a return to base is a documented kind of event (an aircraft taking hits generated a report, a damaged airframe a maintenance record), undated. Ledger #34, issue #130.
